hook_text: Why does the hare have a split lip? One of the oldest stories in Southern Africa says the Moon did it.
clip_script: Full Moon over Cape Town. A storyteller leans in. Long ago, the Moon sent the hare with a message: as I die and come back, so will you. But the hare got it wrong! The Moon was so angry, it split the hare's lip. Around the circle, more stories: a rabbit in the Moon, mooncakes, a crescent that starts Ramadan. Everyone, everywhere, has watched the Moon and told its story.
visual_style: Whiteboard circle of learners around a storyteller under a full Moon, with little pictures floating up: a hare running with a message, a leather shoe flying into the sky, a rabbit in the Moon's patches and a thin crescent above a mosque.
mood: Warm and storytelling, like sitting close together while someone tells a tale.
pacing: Why people everywhere watched the Moon, then stories from Southern Africa, then Moon traditions from around the world and how stories and science fit together.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and ask an older family member for a Moon story.
